subject: Technical deep dive recap: latency/throughput SLOs and deployment topology
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Technical deep dive recap: latency/throughput SLOs and deployment topology

Hi Jordan / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and agreed next steps so we’re all aligned. If anything below reads incorrectly, flag it and I’ll update.

Summary of pain points you described:
- Observed latency spikes during peak hours (p95 and p99 variability) impacting real-time clinical workflows.
- Throughput bottlenecks when concurrent note-generation jobs and embeddings requests overlap.
- Need for predictable tail latency for patient-facing prompts (HIPAA-sensitive).

Goals / success criteria you shared:
- 95th percentile generation latency <= 200ms for typical prompts (~512 tokens)
- Stable throughput of ~200 reqs/sec steady-state, with headroom to burst to 500 reqs/sec for short windows
- Regional (US) deployment with data residency + SOC2/HIPAA controls

Model / inference requirements:
- Mix of instruction-tuned generative models for clinical note generation and smaller embedding models for search/ranking
- Preference for quantized 7B/13B for most requests, with occasional 70B-class model for complex summarization
- Need for streaming responses and support for function/tool calling

Suggested topology we discussed:
- Dedicated Redwood pool (customer-dedicated GPU nodes) in US region for primary traffic
- Autoscaling rules: baseline capacity sized for 200 reqs/sec; burst capacity to absorb 500 reqs/sec for up to 10 minutes
- Fallback route to hosted pool (lower-cost) for non-sensitive workloads or if dedicated capacity is saturated
- KV/prefix caching for repeated prompts (we’ll want sample traffic to verify cache hit rates)

Open items / asks from your side:
1) Sample payloads (typical prompt sizes / average token lengths) and peak hour traffic profile
2) Any regulatory constraints beyond HIPAA (retention windows, specific KMS/HSM requirements)
3) List of 3–4 test prompts to validate tail latency during the deep-dive

Next steps (agreed on call):
- Schedules: Technical deep-dive with our runtime engineer (Dylan) and infra lead (Dev) — propose Wed or Thu next week.
- We’ll share a preliminary sizing spreadsheet and SLA overview (attaching the SLA PDF + sizing workbook).
- You’ll share sample payloads and the traffic profile ahead of the deep-dive.

Attachments: redwood-sla-overview.pdf, acme-sizing.xlsx

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear summary, that matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side:
- The 200 reqs/sec target is for real-time clinician-facing operations; we also run a batched nightly job that can tolerate higher latency but uses the same models.
- Peak bursts are usually tied to shift changes (around 7am/7pm PST) and can last 8–12 minutes.
- We are HIPAA-bound; SOC2 is something we track with vendors — please include SOC2 and relevant attestations in the packet.

We’ll gather representative prompt samples and a 24-hour traffic CSV and send before the deep-dive. Wed (24th) afternoon works for us — can do 1–3pm PT.

Thanks — looping in a few technical notes ahead of the deep-dive.

High-level sizing thoughts based on the numbers Jordan gave:
- Baseline: target steady 200 reqs/sec for 512-token average prompts. With 7B quantized models and batching, we estimate baseline capacity of ~4 x H100-style inference devices (or equivalent A100s) to give consistent p95 < 200ms.
- Burst: allow autoscale to add capacity up to ~8 devices to handle 500 reqs/sec short bursts; pre-warm policy is important to avoid cold-start latency.
- Tail-latency: p99 is heavily impacted by KV cache miss and batch assembly time — we’ll want to test with realistic inter-arrival distributions.

Questions for Jordan (please bring to the deep-dive):
- Typical prompt token distribution (min/median/95th) and embedding request mix (ratio of embedding calls vs generation)
- Are there any hard p99 SLAs or only p95 / business-facing metrics?
- Do you have a preferred KMS vendor for encryption-at-rest?

I attached a quick sizing workbook (acme-sizing.xlsx) to capture the numbers during the session. I’ll prepare a set of benchmark scenarios and a live test plan (latency / throughput / failover) for the meeting.

—Dylan
Principal Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference
